client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: Before leaving the room of a hospitalized client at risk for falls, which action is appropriate?

options.A: Place the call light and needed personal items within the client’s reach.
options.B: Place the call light across the room to encourage independent ambulation.
options.C: Disconnect the call light because frequent calls can interrupt workflow.
options.D: Tell the client to get up independently rather than request assistance.

rationale: AHRQ fall-prevention materials recommend keeping the call light and necessary personal items within reach so the client can request help rather than attempting unsafe unassisted activity.
educational_objective: Maintain access to assistance as an environmental fall-prevention strategy.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
source_document_title: Preventing Falls in Hospitals / Fall Prevention Best Practices
source_locator: Universal fall precautions—necessary items such as call light, telephone, and water within reach
source_claim_supported: Keeping the call light and needed items within reach is part of a safe fall-prevention environment.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Corrected blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety and focused the item on the directly supported fall-prevention action.
audit_findings: Only the correct option supports access to assistance.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
